rounds.text: Oscar Global Ltd is demonstrating accelerating profit growth across multiple horizons, highlighted by a 67% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a 16% compounded growth over 3 years [E8, E9]. This bottom-line expansion is validating recent price performance where profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 12%, signaling that the company is starting to outperform expectations [E30]. Furthermore, fundamental operating results are improving with a net profit increase of 33% year-over-year, supported by a turnaround bias where results score 62 out of 100 while market sentiment remains cautious [E41]. The balance sheet offers robust downside protection, as the company is almost debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and flat borrowings at Rs 0.00 Cr [E23, E24, E32]. Promoter confidence is underscored by a slight increase in holding to 44.06% as of September 2026 [E26]. Conceded: [E5, E6, E20, E21, E22, E35].

The valuation of Oscar Global Ltd is completely disconnected from its underlying profitability, carrying a price-to-book multiple of 2.77x to 2.78x [E1, E33] while sitting at the absolute peak of its 52-week range [E4]. This rich pricing is fundamentally unsupported given that both return on capital employed and return on equity languish at -3.8% [E5, E6], backed by a grim multi-year track record featuring a 10-year median ROE of -23% and a 5-year median ROE of -16% [E14, E15]. Furthermore, operating margins have been on a declining trajectory over the last five years [E18], and the business fails to generate any cash, posting a negative operating and free cash flow of Rs -0.37 Cr for March 2026 [E21, E22]. Compounding these operational weaknesses, the company suffers from a low interest coverage ratio [E34] and pays a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3]. conceded: [E9]

While the bear points to a rich price-to-book multiple of 2.77x [E1] and a 52-week high [E4], the market is properly front-running a powerful fundamental inflection: compounded profit growth has accelerated to 16% over 3 years and an impressive 67% over the trailing twelve months [E8, E9], backed by recent net profit surging 33% year-over-year [E37]. The historical drag in multi-year median ROE [E14, E15] is stale sentiment that ignores a live turnaround, where results score 62 out of 100 and profits are actively outpacing 1-year price growth by 12% [E30, E41]. On the balance sheet risk, the company is almost debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and flat zero borrowings [E23, E24, E32], neutralizing the bear's concern regarding interest coverage [E34]. Furthermore, promoter holdings have ticked up by 0.22 percentage points to 44.06% [E26], signaling insider confidence that aligns with a cyclical earnings profile [E31] outperforming sector median profit growth [E43]. conceded: [E3], [E5], [E6], [E18], [E21], [E22].

The bull highlights accelerated profit growth [E8, E9] and a 33% year-over-year net profit surge [E37] to dismiss historical weaknesses, but this overlooks the reality of negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -0.37 Cr for Mar 2026 [E21, E22]. While the bull frames multi-year median ROE as stale sentiment [E14, E15], the current ROE remains negative at -3.8% [E6] and the yearly operating-margin trend is demonstrably decreasing over the last 5 years [E18]. The argument that zero debt neutralizes interest coverage concerns [E23, E24, E32] ignores the explicit negative flag that the company carries a low interest coverage ratio [E34]. The bull points to promoter accumulation [E26] and improving earnings scores [E41], yet the rules-based screen only scores a neutral 51 out of 100 with explicit warnings that earnings growth is decelerating and ROE remains low [E36, E39, E40]. Furthermore, paying a 2.77x price-to-book multiple [E1] for a stock sitting at 100% of its 52-week range [E4] with a 0.00% dividend yield [E3] and cyclical seasonal weaknesses in Mar, Sep, and Dec [E31] exposes investors to sharp downside when sentiment cools. conceded: [E37], [E41], [E43].
